I've spent more than ten years coaching hockey players, from youth development through to a national team. The one thing I could never give a player on paper was adaptation — the plan that changes when they miss a day, when two games land in one week, when the body says no.
So I built the app to carry the rules I'd use in person. Same sport science, same periodization, built for a 12-year-old's growth spurt and a 40-year-old's knees alike.
M.Ed. Sport ScienceMaster's in PE & Sport Science
Former UAE national-team coachSenior men's ice hockey
1,000+ athletes, 30+ countries60+ went on to sign pro
Exercise selection, loading and rest come from the research on skating speed, change of direction and repeat-sprint ability — not from what looks good on a feed.
Foundation → Strength → Power → Peak, with planned deloads. Volume climbs, unloads, and climbs again so the gains show up on the ice, not just in the gym.
Explosive starts, crossover power, rotational strength for the shot, groin durability, and an engine for the third period. Every session has lateral and rotational work.
From athletes who trained with Elite Hockey Drills programs.
My shot power and acceleration are noticeably different. What I love is that the science is actually explained — I understand why I'm doing each exercise, not just following random routines.

How does the free trial work?

Download the app free, answer five questions, and your personalized season is ready. The 7-day trial unlocks everything — every block, every demo video, progress tracking. Cancel before it ends and you pay nothing. After that it's $99.90/year (about $8.33 a month) or $17.99/month, billed by Apple or Google.

Any hockey player serious about getting better on the ice — competitive youth, juniors, college, adult amateurs, beer league and masters. One app covers every age band from 9–11 through 40+, and every exercise scales easier or harder to your level. For players under 13, a parent sets it up and runs the sessions with them.

Only if you want one. You tell the app what you've got — nothing at all, a band and a box, dumbbells and a pull-up bar, or a full gym — and every session is built from that kit. Full gym? Expect barbells, trap bar and sled work. Hotel room? Bodyweight and a band. Change your equipment any time and the program re-plans around it.
Yes. The app is live on Google Play with the same personalized program, demo videos and 7-day free trial as on iPhone. Get it on Google Play →
App subscription or $79 program — which one?

The app is the full experience: personalized to you, aware of your games, adapts when you miss a day, tracks progress, and keeps going all year. The $79 programs are fixed 8-week blocks you buy once — good if you want one focused block and no subscription. If you're unsure, start the free week first.
What about in-season — I don't have time for 4 sessions a week.

Tell the app where the season stands and it starts there. In-season means two or three lighter, game-day-aware sessions a week plus short pre- and post-game pieces — not an eight-week ramp you don't have time for.

The free week means you try everything before paying a cent, and subscriptions are managed and cancelled through your App Store or Google Play account. The one-time $79 programs have a 30-day money-back guarantee — email and we'll sort it.
Not currently. The app is built to deliver the same systematic approach used with national-level athletes, in a form that fits in your pocket.
